posts.author: levelsio
posts.text:
I think in 10 or 20 years the kitchen and living room combo layout will have disappeared from most homes

Cooking is the primary source of indoor air pollution and you're essentially releasing microscopic toxic gases into your living room and the rest of your house

On top of that 99% of kitchen vents don't do anything

That is, unless we invent some better air cleaning system for kitchens that actually work
posts.text_zh:
我觉得再过 10 到 20 年，开放式厨客厅一体的布局会从大多数家里消失

做饭是室内空气污染的首要来源，你基本上是在往客厅和整栋房子里排放微观有毒气体

更糟的是，99% 的厨房抽油烟机根本没什么用

除非我们发明出真正管用的厨房空气净化系统

posts.author: levelsio
posts.text:
A very tragic crash with a private jet once again

Before this crash the Learjet 60 was had fatal odds per trip of 1 in 1.1 million

To compare a good commercial airline like Delta has a 1 in 25 million odds, many airlines never crashed though so the real odds are even lower like 1 in 40 million trips maybe

So the Learjet 60 was already 40x less safe than commercial airliners

That's something I keep repeating about private jets, they're simply not as safe as flying commercial because:
- pilots require less flight hours
- private aviation is less regulated
- smaller airports with less or no instrument landing systems (ILS)
- smaller planes are more affected by weather (in this case icing)

The Learjet 60 now has fatal odds of 1 in 800,000 which is still about double as safe as the Cessna Citation (one of the most common private jets)

Most Gulfstreams still have flawless safety records though, G500/G600, G550, G650/G700/G800 never crashed, so if you are boarding a private jet anytime soon, I'd say go with them!
posts.text_zh:
又一次私人飞机的惨烈坠机

这次事故前，Learjet 60 每次飞行的致命事故概率约为 110 万分之一

对比一下，像 Delta 这样的好航空公司约为 2500 万分之一；很多航司从未坠毁，真实概率可能更低，比如 4000 万分之一左右

所以 Learjet 60 本来就比民航客机危险大约 40 倍

我一直在强调私人飞机不如民航安全，因为：
- 飞行员所需飞行小时更少
- 私人航空监管更松
- 小机场仪表着陆系统（ILS）更少甚至没有
- 小飞机更易受天气影响（这次是结冰）

现在 Learjet 60 的致命概率变成约 80 万分之一，仍大约是 Cessna Citation（最常见私人机之一）的两倍安全

不过多数 Gulfstream 仍保持完美安全纪录，G500/G600、G550、G650/G700/G800 从未坠毁，所以如果你近期要坐私人飞机，我会建议选它们！

posts.author: levelsio
posts.quoted_text:
Just had a call with a photo editing service which made me realize the second order effect of AI is taking way more jobs. 

HeadshotPro taking photographers jobs, which take away photo editors their jobs which reduces Photoshop licences. Down and down and down.

Gemini now doing photo creation taking our job. 

All in Google it is.
posts.quoted_text_zh:
刚和一家修图服务通完电话，让我意识到 AI 的二阶效应会干掉更多工作。

HeadshotPro 抢走摄影师的活，修图师随之失业，Photoshop 授权减少。一层层往下砍。

现在 Gemini 又在做图片创作，抢走我们的工作。

这些全在 Google 里。
posts.quoted_summary_zh: 被引用帖（@dannypostma）：和修图服务通话后意识到 AI 二阶效应会干掉更多工作——HeadshotPro 抢摄影师、修图师失业、Photoshop 授权下降；Gemini 又在做图，最终都汇到 Google。

posts.author: levelsio
posts.text:
This is correct

Passkeys should be used as passwords, since they're stored in a password manager

They're "supposed" to use biometrics, but realistically they don't, you just unlock your password manager and your passkey is stored there

So passkeys are not 2FA, they're single factor authentication

Prove me wrong
posts.text_zh:
这说得对

Passkeys 应该当密码来用，因为它们存在密码管理器里

它们「理应」用生物识别，但现实里并不是：你只是解锁密码管理器，passkey 就存在那儿

所以 passkeys 不是 2FA，它们是单因素认证

有本事反驳我
posts.quoted_text:
I genuinely struggle to understand  the concept of passkeys and how they are supposed to make things more secure. 

It seems like for some reason most password managers store the passkey in their vault but this then suddenly circumvents the entire concept of 2FA yet again, doesn't it? 

It feels the same as having your auth codes inside your PW manager. 

Am I missing something?
posts.quoted_text_zh:
我真的搞不懂 passkeys 到底怎么让事情更安全。

好像多数密码管理器会把 passkey 存在保险库里，但这又突然绕开了 2FA 的本意，对吧？

感觉和把验证码放进密码管理器一样。

是我漏了什么吗？
posts.quoted_summary_zh: 被引用帖（@sobedominik）质疑 passkey 如何更安全：多数密码管理器把 passkey 存在保险库里，这又绕开了 2FA 的本意，感觉和把验证码放进密码管理器一样。

posts.author: marclou
posts.text:
The creator of Naruto @TheKishimoto was writing in public!

Every few pages in the manga, he shares a little story: a challenge he faced while drawing a character, a sketch of his desk, or even a story about his childhood.

It’s so interesting. It builds a connection between us.

I think every creator (writers, actors, entrepreneurs) should embed their DNA in their work.

AI can’t replace that.
posts.text_zh:
《火影忍者》作者 @TheKishimoto 居然在公开写作！

漫画每隔几页，他就会分享一段小故事：画某个角色时遇到的挑战、自己书桌的速写，甚至童年往事。

太有意思了。这会在我们和他之间建立起连接。

我觉得每个创作者（写作者、演员、创业者）都应该把自己的 DNA 嵌进作品里。

AI 替代不了这一点。
posts.quoted_text: Re-reading Naruto as an adult feels like being 12 again for a little while.
posts.quoted_text_zh: 成年后再读《火影忍者》，短暂感觉自己又变回了 12 岁。

Observation: the smarter everything gets, the more valuable dumbness becomes. 

I think “offline” is about to become a luxury feature, the way a mechanical watch or a paper notebook became a  status signal once everything else went digital.
